data.notes: The report's strongest point is the core story: we won the CTO with technical proof and lost the COO, who was buying people and an outage plan. It ties Halima's 'queue with a faster timer' and 'I don't buy uptime' lines to four well-aimed messaging changes, and it labels the over-promise claim as unverified opinion. It misses the key's competitor (Checkout.com) and incumbent (an in-house bank gateway), though neither is named in the transcript, so the report's null/unnamed answers are faithful to the source. Its close also omits commercial terms and whether we could offer named on-sale coverage, and wrongly calls the plan question 'dodged' when the rep answered it. The first messaging change writes copy that promises a named SE, an account lead and a shared channel without evidence that we can staff them.
